shortcuts_and_limits: One API process with SQLite and an in-process worker; no distributed worker or shared in-memory locks.
Local password accounts have no email verification or password recovery.
Login limits use the transport client address and ignore forwarded headers; shared proxy addresses share a limit.
Workspace bounds use the latest 1000 distinct eligible reviews, isolated by owner, workspace, decision type and model identity; legacy unproven reviews do not unlock owned workspaces.
Spot-check counters remain in-process, as before; review evidence, history, switches, action claims and audit records persist.
Local reader files must be immutable while running and require restart after replacement; fingerprints cover every saved file.

Remote requests contain at most 1000 current history rows before endpoint nearest-eight retrieval; corrections move to the recent end. Revision pinning is optional; an unpinned changed revision needs new evidence.
An unresolved remote revision cannot use evidence until a successful response supplies its identity. Network failures never authorize an automatic action.
Typed readers have no inherited public benchmark certificate. The existing 99% promotion gate is unchanged.
Separate Ads workspaces use the existing four-action labels; inbox options remain approved verbatim response templates, without freeform generation.
Only operator-allowed sandbox Ads accounts are supported. No Meta account-management writes are implemented.
Meta app-level webhook setup and permissions remain operator tasks; asset subscription failures preserve selections. Old inventories missing parent IDs require reconnecting.
Unsubscribe is best effort; local credentials/mappings are erased on disconnect even when provider cleanup fails. Meta app roles are not revoked.
Observed outcomes still need human review before training; hindsight reviews do not unlock Act and observations do not establish causation.
Answer undo cannot retract delivered messages. Ads undo refuses intervening target changes, claims atomically and leaves ambiguous results for manual review.
Global stop cannot cancel a provider request already submitted. Stops are rechecked after Ads snapshot reads and before undo claims.
Deleted workspace names remain blocked for the process lifetime to reject stale requests; choose a new name or restart.

The Modal SDK is an optional operator tool, outside app runtime dependencies. The GPU image follows the existing pinned Torch image pattern; no GPU deployment/runtime or latency verification was performed.
The load probe was not run. It uses fixed arrivals and concurrent requests, nearest-rank latency over all attempts, and no retries; no capacity measurement is claimed.
Cached packages were used with UV_NO_SYNC=true; no dependency install, lockfile change or Dockerfile change was needed.
No live OAuth, Meta delivery, browser or GPU execution was performed; no paid calls. Runtime tests use mocked models and transports.
Frontend, submission docs and seeded demo are owned elsewhere and were not edited; the frontend owner must consume the new basis/subscription metadata. Six existing frontend lint warnings remain.
